💡 Key Takeaways
  • Amazon is taking its fight against a Latest York City delivery bill, which has been backed by Mayor Zohran Mamdani, to its shopping website and app.
  • Some people who open the company's shopping app or website report being served with pop-ups and banners warning that the Upcoming York City Council "could add up to $5 per order" if it passes Intro 518, or the Delivery Protection Act.
  • Industry observers note that the bill would require Amazon to employ its army of third-party delivery companies directly, disrupting the contractor model it has relied on since 2018.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Amazon is taking its fight against a Latest York City delivery bill, which has been backed by Mayor Zohran Mamdani, to its shopping website and app.

Some people who open the company's shopping app or website report being served with pop-ups and banners warning that the Upcoming York City Council "could add up to $5 per order" if it passes Intro 518, or the Delivery Protection Act.

Industry observers note that the bill would require Amazon to employ its army of third-party delivery companies directly, disrupting the contractor model it has relied on since 2018. Amazon uses a network of thousands of small companies, which often work solely for Amazon, to handle the last-mile portion of shipments, in an effort to speed up deliveries and control more of its logistics operations.

"If this legislation passes, we'd no longer be able to work with them, and we'd be forced to consider moving our operations outside of the city," Amazon's in-app message states. "That would likely mean slower and more expensive delivery for millions of customers in Fresh York City, while also threatening small businesses and their thousands of employees.".

The proposed legislation was introduced in February and is awaiting review by City Council Speaker Julie Menin.

Amazon also posted a statement on its company website where it often publishes its policy positions. But rarely has the company used its valuable e-commerce site and app real estate to push its perspectives. Other tech companies including Uber and Lyft have similarly used their apps to advocate for or against legislation in the past.

Amazon's pop-up notices and a stationary banner on its store homepage direct users to a form where they can "contact your council member to oppose Intro 518.".

According to Amazon, 20,000 customers sent emails to city council members in the first six hours that the pop-up appeared.

Menin told CNBC in a statement that Amazon's claim it will need to raise prices due to the proposed legislation "defies logic.".

Sources indicate that "We are crafting legislation that regulates Amazon and protects workers, without impacting prices or jobs," Menin noted. "If Amazon thinks this deceptive campaign will effectively threaten Newly introduced Yorkers and intimidate this City Council, they are dead wrong.".

Amazon spokesperson Kelly Nantel noted in a statement that the firm put up the notices to be "transparent with our customers" about what the bill "would cause them if it passes as written.".

"If customers are concerned, one of the most impactful things they can do is contact their City Council member and ask them to oppose this bill," Nantel noted.

The Delivery Protection Act has received a swell of support from labor groups, including the International Brotherhood of Teamsters, which has sought to unionize Amazon delivery and warehouse workers.

Mamdani endorsed the bill in August, saying Amazon's subcontractor model "leaves workers vulnerable and corporations free to avoid accountability for reckless conditions on city streets." He's argued the bill would lead to safer working conditions for drivers, and allow the city to "regulate last-mile operations.".

Amazon disputed Mamdani's claims, saying the bill would put Delivery Service Partner jobs "at risk without improving safety." It also argued that other businesses and governments use contractors in their operations, and remarked the DSP model has allowed it to meet growing customer demand.

In a recent development, "It works because local entrepreneurs — people rooted in their communities — deliver a better experience," Amazon said. "They invest in their teams, their routes, and their neighborhoods. That's not a liability play.".

Amazon has lobbied heavily against the bill, while logistics and business groups have launched local advertising campaigns, and warned they may sue the city if the bill passes.

You can shoot basketball, play pool, enjoy video games, and so much more that is actually related to missions and the story itself.

Recent findings suggest that but 2013's Grand Theft Auto V was a good-looking, immersive game for its time as well. So we took some time to compare how the games react in similar situations.

It has been revealed that what happens when you shoot a window? What happens if you beat up a car? Basically, we tested some of the little things you can do in GTA 5 and GTA 6 between missions out of sheer curiosity.

When attempting to shoot car windows in both games, windshields tested did not shatter completely in GTA 6, while the damage appears slightly more detailed in GTA 5. Both games had car windows shatter in similarly reactive ways.

Industry observers note that with building windows and glass doors, GTA 5 actually performed better, shattering and breaking apart when shot. In GTA 6, the windows did not shatter when shot, despite throwing an explosion of glass shards where the bullets struck.

Beating up cars reacted similarly in both games, though I'd say GTA 6 veers much closer to realism and gives the impression of weight being thrown into the strikes.

And if you're just trying to take in the vibes rather than smashing things, you can go to the water's edge and watch the sunset. This is just my opinion, but GTA 6's sunset is gorgeous to watch and is absolutely a vibe.

But you don't have to take my word for it; you can see the side-by-side comparisons for yourself.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that microsoft is saying goodbye to its task management service To Do, including the Mac and iOS apps.
  • The last day to use the To Do apps is June 30, 2027.
  • “Microsoft To Do is retiring,” Microsoft explains.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that microsoft is saying goodbye to its task management service To Do, including the Mac and iOS apps. Here’s what users need to know.

The last day to use the To Do apps is June 30, 2027. That date also applies to Windows, Android, and the web. The underlying service and sync support will retire later, according to Microsoft’s support document.

“Microsoft To Do is retiring,” Microsoft explains. “For work or school accounts, Microsoft Planner will be the destination for managing personal work tasks alongside assigned work. The updated My tasks experience begins rolling out in December 2026.”.

On the Mac, you can use Planner on the web or in Teams. Microsoft explicitly says it has no looks for a native Mac app.

You can still see your existing To Do tasks in Planner through June 30, but your tasks and lists won’t carry over. Microsoft plans to offer an export option before the apps retire.

Planner doesn’t support personal Microsoft accounts however. If that’s how you use To Do, you’ll need to pick another task manager, even if you pay for Microsoft 365 Personal or Family, according to the manufacturer.

The June shutdown will end a run of just over a decade for To Do on Apple platforms. Microsoft bought the company behind Wunderlist in 2015 and released the first iPhone preview of To Do in April 2017.

Recent findings suggest that looking for a proper replacement? Apple’s built-in Reminders app can keep lists in sync between Apple devices, including a grocery list you share with family through iCloud.

If you liked To Do because it worked across platforms, Todoist has apps for iPhone, iPad, Mac, Windows, and Android.

In a recent development, does this sunsetting affect you? Were you a Wunderlist user back in the day? Share your thoughts in the comments.

  • The report claims that "after the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shares of chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices close down 7.72% to $489.19 Thursday after investment firm Hunterbrook Media issued a report alleging that the manufacturer "has its own China problem.".

Hunterbrook disclosed that it had taken a short position in AMD.

The report claims that "after the U.S. blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, the tech giant kept getting newer AMD firmware, which enables AMD chips to run in servers.".

CNBC did not independently verify this information.

Hunterbrook also said that new export rules in Washington could "tighten restrictions on AMD's foreign business," alleging that AMD "bills over 20% of its revenue to customers in China and Hong Kong," and "depends on a Chinese partner to finish most of its chips.".

Recent findings suggest that the allegations come amid investigations of rival chipmaker Nvidia over its sales to companies in Asia with ties to China. AMD has been viewed as a beneficiary of the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia.

In a recent development, "The claims misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships," an AMD spokesperson stated in a statement. "AMD complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations. We remain focused on serving our customers and upholding the highest standards of integrity.".

Industry observers note that lisa Su, CEO of AMD, told investors on the company's recent earnings call that China is an "notable" market and that the semiconductor giant wants to be fully compliant with U.S. export controls.

AMD continued to slide after-hours, trading down 0.45% to $487 shortly after 4 p.m.

30 gifts for the outdoorsy folks in your life

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (495 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Do you know someone who basically lives at the local climbing gym?
  • Industry observers note that if any of these groups sound like you or someone you know, you've been exposed to the granola lifestyle.
  • Outdoorsy folk have taken to TikTok with the hashtags #granolagirl, #granolaboy, and #granolacheck over the last few years to show off their adventurous, outdoor-oriented lifestyles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Do you know someone who basically lives at the local climbing gym? Are you friends with a person whose only personality trait is taking their dog hiking? Or maybe your partner is obsessed with the idea of living in a van (#vanlife) and traveling the country?

Industry observers note that if any of these groups sound like you or someone you know, you've been exposed to the granola lifestyle. Similar to gorpcore, folks who fit the granola aesthetic are typically into camping, hiking, and kayaking, and have probably talked about moving to Colorado one day (guilty). They love to be outdoors, sip craft beer, and of course, wear Patagonia fleece sweaters.

Outdoorsy folk have taken to TikTok with the hashtags #granolagirl, #granolaboy, and #granolacheck over the last few years to show off their adventurous, outdoor-oriented lifestyles. For many, getting into nature was a direct response to feeling cooped up during the lockdowns of the early pandemic. But that trend is here to stay.

For people who are unsure about adventure gear themselves but still want to find the perfect granola gift this holiday season, we chatted with outdoor expert and REI soft goods Lead and Virtual Outfitter Mike Kreis for some outdoor gear shopping tips.

Kreis suggests that you consider how long your giftee has been into their activity, whether it's hiking, skiing, camping, or climbing. "The longer they have been doing the activity, the more gear they will have," he claims.

According to recent reports, if your gift recipient already owns some gear, Kreis states it's best to go for nonessentials. "I always like to go with items that aren't necessarily needed for the activity, as they most likely have that," he says. So opt for a portable charger, a cozy outdoor blanket, or extra camp cooking gadgets. Really, anything that can make outdoor life more comfortable will make a great gift.

According to recent reports, if you find yourself shopping for the outdoorsy person in your life, look no further. We've rounded up 30 of the best presents out there, whether their version of adventure is having a picnic in the park or roughing it in the back country.

Palo Alto stock jumps on earnings beat and company's big bet on securing open-weight models

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (339 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Palo Alto Networks shares rose 6% on Thursday as businesses boosted spending on cybersecurity products and investors cheered the organization's acquisition of a startup that pushes it into securing open-weight artificial intelligence models.
  • The manufacturer beat Wall Street's estimates for the fiscal first quarter.
  • Sources indicate that recent outages at Microsoft, banks and the Federal Aviation Administration have left businesses reeling.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Palo Alto Networks shares rose 6% on Thursday as businesses boosted spending on cybersecurity products and investors cheered the organization's acquisition of a startup that pushes it into securing open-weight artificial intelligence models.

The manufacturer beat Wall Street's estimates for the fiscal first quarter. Revenue jumped 39% from a year ago and Palo Alto lifted its guidance for the year.

Sources indicate that recent outages at Microsoft, banks and the Federal Aviation Administration have left businesses reeling. While U.S. officials haven't detected any malicious activity, the disruptions raise concerns over aging equipment and infrastructure. Many businesses are scrambling to patch vulnerabilities at a faster clip than ever before to keep pace with the growing risks of AI-powered cyberattacks.

Those fears have led more businesses to consolidate platforms, which is fueling growth in areas like firewall and AI security, Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora told CNBC's "Mad Money" on Wednesday.

"They're going to have to make sure they get the best players in the market to come support them because this is no longer child's play," Arora stated.

Alongside earnings, Palo Alto confirmed a $4.5 billion deal to buy Applied Compute, a startup that helps train customized open-weight models. It's one of several recent deals in Arora's aggressive acquisition spree and marks a significant shift beyond cybersecurity.

"Rather than being one player out of 10 in the industry serving compute, we want to be the one player with Palo Alto that delivers secure compute and security capability," Arora told CNBC.

Palo Alto expects the deal to add more than $1 billion in annual recurring revenue to its next-generation security business by the 2029 fiscal year.

Analysts at Bank of America touted the deal as a "bold move" to expand beyond securing AI into training open-weight models, allowing Palo Alto to lead the next phase of the AI revolution.

This "appears consistent with PANW's 'long-game' - become indispensable beyond cyber into multidisciplinary IT domains across AI-value-chain," wrote analysts at Citigroup.

Purchases accounted for at least $29.2 million and sales at least $11.7 million. The filing reports transactions in broad dollar ranges, leaving the exact amounts and value of Trump's holdings unclear.

Among the transactions were Palantir purchases before the company received two federal contracts worth $42.5 million combined, according to contracting records, SpaceX investments shortly before and after a $946 million NASA contract expansion, and Nvidia trades as its then-CEO, Jensen Huang, cultivated a close relationship with Trump.

Recent findings suggest that the trades underscore a striking feature of Trump's presidency: His personal fortune remains invested in companies whose fortunes his administration can shape. His accounts reported more than 21,000 trades in 2025, compared with roughly 500 during his entire first term. Recent presidents have generally divested individual stocks or used blind trusts to avoid potential conflicts.

The White House has told CNBC previously Trump and his family have no control over the trades, which outside financial managers handle independently. The Trump Organization indicates the arrangement is designed to avoid even the appearance of a conflict. There is no evidence Trump directed the transactions or that his managers knew government decisions in advance.

Sources indicate that white House spokesman Davis Ingle said that Trump's portfolio is independently managed and that neither the president nor his family has any input on trades. "All investment decisions are made entirely by independent managers," Ingle told CNBC.

The Trump Organization did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Sources indicate that the timing was particularly notable at Palantir, the artificial intelligence software maker whose technology is used by U.S. military, intelligence and civilian agencies.

Trump's accounts bought between $15,001 and $50,000 in Palantir shares on Sept. 2, followed by another purchase of between $1,001 and $15,000 on Sept. 9.

A week later, the Department of Housing and Urban Development awarded Palantir a contract with $10.4 million in initial obligations for AI-powered grant oversight and fraud detection.

Sources indicate that on Sept. 29, the Department of Homeland Security awarded Palantir another $32.1 million software contract, bringing the two awards to roughly $42.5 million. That same day, CEO Alex Karp joined Trump, Musk, Huang and other technology executives at the White House for a meeting on artificial intelligence.

Trump's accounts also bought shares and debt in SpaceX in the weeks surrounding a major NASA contract award.

Recent findings suggest that on Sept. 1, the accounts purchased between $100,001 and $250,000 in SpaceX debt carrying a 5.35% interest rate. Eight days later, they bought between $1,001 and $15,000 in shares of the major NASA and Pentagon contractor.

On Sept. 18, NASA announced a $946 million expansion of its SpaceX contract, adding three astronaut missions to the International Space Station and bringing the agreement's total value to $5.92 billion. The agency had signaled intends for additional missions in May.

Six days after the announcement, Trump's accounts bought another $15,001 to $50,000 in SpaceX shares on the same day Musk attended Trump's White House state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping. The filing does not show whether the purchase came before or after the dinner.

The trades followed an even larger SpaceX investment in August, when Trump's accounts bought between $1 million and $5 million in the company's debt just two days before he signed a policy aimed at expanding commercial space transportation.

Trump's accounts also continued buying Nvidia shares as Huang drew closer to the president — a relationship now under congressional scrutiny over Huang's ties to a woman suspected of spying for China.

Recent findings suggest that the September filing demonstrates four Nvidia purchases totaling between $152,004 and $380,000, including two on Sept. 2 worth as much as $350,000 combined.

The accounts also sold between $1,001 and $15,000 in Nvidia shares on Sept. 24, the day Huang also attended the state dinner with Xi.

The trades bring Trump's Nvidia transactions to at least 108 since his return to office in 2025, worth between $27.2 million and $97.9 million, extending a CNBC analysis published Monday.

Recent findings suggest that the relationship between the president and Nvidia's then-CEO has drawn fresh scrutiny after The Upcoming York Times reported that intelligence officials warned Trump about Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. Trump has denied being briefed. Huang resigned Nov. 12 following revelations about his personal relationships.

Sources indicate that the September filing also shows substantial trading beyond the three companies. The largest reported transaction was a Sept. 23 purchase of between $5 million and $25 million in Vanguard Dividend Appreciation ETF shares.

That same day, Trump's accounts sold between $1 million and $5 million each in Comcast, McDonald's, Home Depot and Fidelity National Information Services, along with between $500,001 and $1 million each in Nike and Constellation Brands.

According to recent reports, on the buy side, Trump's accounts purchased between $250,001 and $500,000 in TJX shares on each of two consecutive days, Sept. 15 and 16. They also bought between $117,004 and $330,000 in Tesla shares across four transactions, along with smaller investments in CoreWeave, Intel, Microsoft and Apple.

Sources indicate that the Elec reported on Thursday that Apple is considering delaying or even canceling a hypothetical OLED-equipped iMac model, which was theoretically supposed to launch in 2029 or 2030. According to the report, which cited an unnamed industry source, Apple has been working with Samsung Display (a prolific supplier of device displays) on the project, and has been discussing a potential delay or cancellation with the Korean firm.

Sources indicate that unsurprisingly, money seems like the biggest factor here. Apple is reportedly concerned about the cost of equipping its all-in-one desktop computers with fancy (but expensive) OLED displays, given that iMacs don't sell at nearly the same volume as some of Apple's other flagship products, like the iPhone. The Elec also cited weak sales of the iPad Pro, which has a ProMotion OLED display, as a factor here. iOS 27 gave AirPods Pro a variety of new features, but there’s another addition that’s easy to miss: a convenient new setting in Control Center for Adaptive Audio.

Several AirPods models offer excellent Active Noise Cancellation and Transparency modes—especially AirPods Pro 3 (now only $179).

But Adaptive Audio is another option you may or may not have tried. The feature aims to blend the strengths of both ANC and Transparency in a single mode.

And in iOS 27, Apple added a new setting to let you conveniently fine-tune Adaptive Audio to your preferences.

It has been revealed that while wearing AirPods, open Control Center on your iPhone and tap the volume slider, then hit ‘Listening Mode’ in the bottom-left corner. Here you’ll see the standard listening mode options.

Upcoming in iOS 27 though, when ‘Adaptive’ is selected, you can now use a Liquid Glass slider to adjust whether the mode lets in more or less external noise.

Slide it to the left and Adaptive Audio will more closely resemble Transparency, while sliding it to the right makes it cancel out more noise.

According to recent reports, you can also move the latest slider incrementally to achieve exactly your ideal balance of Transparency and Noise Cancellation. It’s not limited to just a few preset options.

This Control Center slider is available on all AirPods models that support Adaptive Audio.

Do you ever use Adaptive Audio, and if so, have you adjusted it at all? Let us know in the comments.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Payward, the owner of crypto exchange Kraken, is pushing into private markets with its latest acquisition, underscoring a broader shift in cryptocurrencies, from trading-led growth to the buildout of financial infrastructure.
  • According to recent reports, payward remarked late Wednesday that it's buying venture capital and asset management provider Tribe Capital Management, led by Payward's co-CEO Arjun Sethi.
  • Tribe, where Sethi is co-founder and chairman, invests across early- and late-stage private companies and has $2.7 billion in assets under management.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Payward, the owner of crypto exchange Kraken, is pushing into private markets with its latest acquisition, underscoring a broader shift in cryptocurrencies, from trading-led growth to the buildout of financial infrastructure.

According to recent reports, payward remarked late Wednesday that it's buying venture capital and asset management provider Tribe Capital Management, led by Payward's co-CEO Arjun Sethi. No purchase price was disclosed.

Tribe, where Sethi is co-founder and chairman, invests across early- and late-stage private companies and has $2.7 billion in assets under management.

Sources indicate that "Joining Payward gives us the opportunity to bring Tribe's investment approach to a global financial platform," Jonathan Hsu, another co-founder of Tribe Capital, remarked in a statement. "We see a strong fit between our investment approach and Payward's infrastructure, distribution, and product-building capabilities.".

Payward didn't respond to a request for comment.

Recent findings suggest that the acquisition is novel among crypto exchanges. Unlike exchange-owned venture arms such as Coinbase Ventures or Binance Labs, Payward is looking to integrate Tribe's investment and fund-management capabilities into an existing custody, trading, collateral and tokenization infrastructure to develop private-market investment products.

Payward is trying to position itself to capture value from a broader crypto-driven transformation of financial services, not use the venture vehicle to draw more capital into the crypto ecosystem.

The acquisition is another step in the evolution in the crypto exchange business model. With cryptocurrency prices continuing to decline this year, crypto exchanges have worked to move past their reliance on trading volumes and transaction fees, focusing instead on building the infrastructure connecting digital assets with traditional finance.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the first time Amy Poehler and Mike Schur teamed up for a series about Poehler rolling up her sleeves and getting to work in a massive dirt pit, they gave us Parks and Recreation, a charming workplace sitcom about the power of friendship and doing what you love. The second time Amy Poehler and Mike Schur teamed up for a series about Poehler rolling up her sleeves and getting to work in a massive dirt pit, they gave us Peacock's fresh series Dig, which is — you guessed it! — a charming workplace sitcom about the power of friendship and doing what you love.

Story-wise, the two demonstrates are miles apart. Literally. The former takes place in the decidedly unglamorous town of Pawnee, Indiana, while the latter, based on Kate Myers' novel Excavations, transports us to a sun-bleached archaeological dig in Greece. Yet despite the flashy location and a new mystery twist, Dig retains the core formula that made Parks and Recreation so irresistible: investing deeply in a lovable new crew of unlikely friends.

Kicking off that group is Elise (Poehler), the lead archaeologist on a long-running dig in southern Greece. She's qualified and passionate, yet has a hard time connecting with the undergraduates (or UGs) participating in the dig. Because of her more guarded exterior, she's consistently second fiddle to longtime dig leader Neville (Hugh Laurie). Perpetually on the brink of retirement, Neville seems unable to cede control of the dig to Elise, both because of his love for archaeology and the ego boost his role gives him. He's the Lucy to Elise's Charlie Brown, constantly yanking the football away at the last second.

Recent findings suggest that so, when Elise discovers a perfectly preserved statue of Hera at an older dig site, the last thing she wants to do is tell Neville and give him an opportunity to claim any shred of credit. However, hiding any cultural artifacts from Neville and the Grecian government at large is illegal, so Elise must assemble a crack team to help her cover up her covert dig of the Hera statue, whom they nickname "Pretty Woman." First up is Dylan (Geraldine Viswanathan), an always flaky wild card who has unfinished business at the dig. Joining her are Clare (Antonia Thomas), a prim and proper conservator born with a silver spoon in her mouth, and Patty (Fina Strazza), a sheltered farm girl with a deep passion for Greek mythology.

Like with most sitcoms, the characters begin as the broadest versions of themselves before revealing their deeper nuances. At first, Elise is prickly to a fault, allowing Poehler to sidestep any preconceived comparisons you might want to draw to Leslie Knope. Elsewhere, Dylan is the hottest of hot messes, Clare is a haughty queen bee, and Patty is an out-of-her-depth klutz. They border on parodies instead of full-bodied characters, making Dig's earlier episodes a bit lukewarm.

It has been revealed that but as Dig's title suggests, this is a show that won't be satisfied by sticking at surface level. As the show delves into what makes its characters tick, it becomes a heartwarming tale of found family, not unlike many other beloved Schur highlights. Suddenly, character traits that felt one-note to start are revealed to be defense mechanisms or misconceptions, adding entirely upcoming dimensions to Dig's core four.

Recent findings suggest that dig works best when that core works together in earnest, which is another reason why the show's early entries feel like slower burns: They're doing the groundwork to loop every woman into the Pretty Woman dig. Once they're all on the same page, Dig gets off and running — even more so once Pretty Woman mysteriously vanishes, leaving Elise and her motley crew to do some boots-on-the-ground detective work. Thus begins a madcap caper involving stakeouts, undercover identities, and the black market.

Along the way, Elise, Dylan, Clare, and Patty are allowed to be wonderfully messy and vulnerable, all while staying refreshingly supportive of one another. For example, a love triangle burbles up between Clare, Dylan, and Clare's fiancé/Dylan's ex-boyfriend Gary (Jon Pointing), yet the storyline never devolves into cat fights or possessiveness. Instead, Dig focuses more on what these relationships mean to Clare and Dylan beyond romance. For Clare, her engagement is a sign of stability and true adulthood, whereas Dylan is looking for closure, something she notoriously can never get.

Dig also dabbles in intergenerational conflict, highlighting the differences between each of its leads, all of whom are at very different stages in their lives. Again, Dig doesn't take a hackneyed "Gen Z versus millennials versus Gen X" route. It's more interested in showing the different wants that motivate us. Patty yearns for belonging and friendship, while Elise wants to cement her legacy and make sure she's done something big enough to call her own, no Neville required.

Once Dig's ensemble truly comes together, they mesh wonderfully. Poehler brings a weary exasperation to Elise that slowly gives way to warm leadership, a transformation that's a joy to witness. Thomas and Viswanathan are perfect foils, the former a picture of poise, the latter completely uninhibited. Watching them feed off each other offers up a perfect comedic contrast. Finally, there's Strazza, whose endearingly goofy Patty becomes the beating heart of the show. Laurie, too, is a joy, blending Neville's smarminess with a genial charm that makes him infuriatingly tough to hate.

In focusing on archaeology, Dig emphasizes the importance of excavating ancient objects and interrogating the stories of those who once used them. In many ways, Dig is doing the same thing with its characters: peeling back their layers to get at their core truths. Only instead of using trowels and brushes, Dig uses the power of the workplace sitcom. It's a power Schur and his collaborators know well, and the result is a show that will leave you feeling like you've just uncovered something great in a dig of your own — with far less dirt on your face and clothes, that is.

Industry observers note that dec. 1 is officially turning into a fast-food holiday turf war. Just days after McDonald’s revealed its Home Alone meal with collectible socks for Dec. 1, Burger King fired back with a nostalgia-heavy Peanuts holiday menu launching on the same day.

Arriving at participating U.S. restaurants on Dec. 1 (while supplies last), the limited-time Burger King x Peanuts collab introduces two distinct meals: the adult-sized Peanuts Pack and a Peanuts-Inspired King Jr. Meal. Both meals are served inside a collectible Snoopy Doghouse Box.

Choice of Entrée — A classic flame-grilled Whopper with Cheese or 10-piece Chicken Nuggets served with Woodstock Golden Ranch.

Charlie Brown Loaded Potato Tots — Crispy, coin-shaped tots filled with melty cheese, savory bacon bits, sour cream, chives, and fluffy potatoes.

Medium Soft Drink — Choice of medium fountain beverage.

Snoopy Holiday Beanie — One of two limited-edition Snoopy holiday beanies.

It has been revealed that the Peanuts-Inspired King Jr. Meal includes:.

Choice of Entrée — Hamburger, Cheeseburger, or 4-piece Chicken Nuggets.

Side — Choice of Applesauce or French Fries.

Drink — Choice of Milk or Apple Juice.

Peanuts Collectible Toy — One of eight collectible holiday Peanuts toys in every meal, featuring Charlie Brown, Lucy, Linus, Sally, three festive Snoopy designs, and a Snoopy Doghouse packed with custom stickers for decorating.

For collectors, the adult knit beanies and the eight King Jr. Meal toys are especially interesting. Supplies will be limited, and, much like the McDonald's collectible Home Alone socks, fans will scramble to collect them all.

Recent findings suggest that "Peanuts has been part of holiday family traditions for generations, and we can't wait to bring Snoopy and the gang to Burger King this holiday season," noted Joel Yashinsky, Chief Marketing Officer, Burger King U.S. and Canada. "At BK, we go all out on partnerships to create fun experiences for everyone — with new menu items, creative packaging and crowns, collectible Snoopy beanies and Peanuts toys and more, we've created something really special. It's holiday fun for all, and we can't wait to welcome families and fans to BK to celebrate throughout the month of December!".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google Fi Wireless is the latest first-party app to adopt a floating toolbar as part of a small navigation redesign.

In a recent development, previously, the companion app still used a tall Material 3 bottom bar. With the network switching update revealed last week, Google Fi now has a floating navigation toolbar.

The tabs remain Home, Plan, Billing, Shop, and Support. A pill-shaped tab indicator is leveraged, while there’s a prominent shadow effect. Given the floating nature, you see what’s around the toolbar, while Fi Wireless now extends underneath the system navigation bar.

However, the Shop tab loads a webpage as before, resulting in a gap and wasted space.

Industry observers note that there’s now a floating action button for the fresh Google AI-powered Ask Fi chatbot. It provides “instant account help and troubleshooting.” If you ask for human support, the contents of the conversation carry over.

Sources indicate that this redesign is rolling out with version 171 of the app as a server-side upgrade. Google Fi joins Google Photos, Chat, and Pixel Now Playing in adopting floating navigation, which is likely the new first-party mandate for a more edge-to-edge design.

Secondary network switching is not yet widely available, with Google telling us last week that it’s a gradual rollout. The MVNO is also ending Pixel exclusivity for Wi-Fi Auto Connect+ with availability on “select” Samsung and Motorola phones.

Change these Xbox Series X/S settings before playing GTA 6

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (672 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • From calibrating HDR to increasing refresh rate, here's how to get the best GTA VI experience on your Xbox Series X/S.
  • Grand Theft Auto VI is coming out on November 19 on the PlayStation 5 and the Xbox Series X/S.
  • That means that some of the settings on Microsoft's console matter more than usual, if you want the best possible experience out of the game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From calibrating HDR to increasing refresh rate, here's how to get the best GTA VI experience on your Xbox Series X/S.

Grand Theft Auto VI is coming out on November 19 on the PlayStation 5 and the Xbox Series X/S. We have already covered all the settings you need to change on the PlayStation 5 before the game comes out, and now it's the Xbox's turn. The Xbox store page also carries the "Optimized for Xbox Series X|S" badge, meaning the game is built to lean on the console's advanced features.

That means that some of the settings on Microsoft's console matter more than usual, if you want the best possible experience out of the game. Some of them are actual setting toggles inside the console, and some are just about where you install the game. Here is what is worth checking on your Xbox Series X/S before launch night.

Before changing anything, go to Settings > General > TV and Display Options > 4K TV Details. You should see a group of green checkmarks on the screen. According to Microsoft, these checkmarks indicate that everything is working, and it's the quickest way to learn whether your TV and HDMI port can handle the console's best features. Microsoft mentions that the Xbox's most advanced features need an HDMI 2.1 connection. Keep in mind that on some TVs, only certain HDMI ports support 2.1. So make sure you reserve the best port for your Xbox.

Next, open Video Modes in the same menu, and check "Allow variable refresh rate" and "Allow auto low latency mode." Variable refresh rate, or VRR, lets the TV match its refresh rate to the frames the Xbox is producing, which reduces stutter and screen tearing for a much smoother experience. "Allow auto low latency mode," or ALLM, switches the TV into its game mode automatically, which reduces the amount of post-processing your TV does and shortens the delay between what is happening in the game and what you see on screen.

In Video Modes, make sure "Allow HDR10" is checked, then run the Calibrate HDR for Games tool, which fine-tunes HDR to your specific screen. The goal is for bright and dark areas to keep their detail on your particular TV.

Sources indicate that xbox also supports Dolby Vision for gaming, which is available on both the Xbox Series X and S. It requires a Dolby Vision-supported TV and works best with VRR and ALLM switched on. Over a hundred games are presently optimized for Dolby Vision HDR and Dolby Atmos, and GTA VI will be joining them at launch with calibrated Dolby support. Check whether your TV supports these Dolby formats by going through your TV's display and audio settings, and get the best possible experience.

In a recent development, this one is very important. Games that are optimized for the Series X and S can only be played from the internal SSD or an official storage expansion card. An external USB drive (even an SSD) can hold the game files, but the game will not run unless the entire game is on the internal SSD or expansion card. Considering the fact that GTA 6's download file is reported to be a whopping 212GB, and that the Series S is equipped with an internal SSD with capacity as low as 512GB, you are going to need as much of that storage free as possible. You can go to Settings > Storage and start deleting the games and files you can live without, or perhaps move them to a USB storage.

Preloading on Xbox began on November 10, and if you have already pre-ordered the game, it might be a good idea to preload it on your console so you don't have to start downloading over 200GB and moving files on the day the game comes out. Change all of these settings, and you will give the game its best chance of looking as good as possible once Grand Theft Auto VI finally arrives.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that on Thursday, Nov.
  • ET, AO3 confirmed the disruption, attributing it to preventative maintenance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Archive of Our Own (AO3) is down again, just four days after the popular fanfiction platform came back online after a prolonged outage that left millions of readers scrambling for alternatives.

Industry observers note that on Thursday, Nov. 19, people began reporting problems accessing the site, with outage-tracking website Downdetector showing a spike in reports beginning around 6:08 a.m. ET.

At 6:27 a.m. ET, AO3 confirmed the disruption, attributing it to preventative maintenance.

Sources indicate that "AO3 is down for preventative maintenance," the platform wrote in an upgrade. "We apologize for the inconvenience, and will provide updates when we have them.".

The latest downtime comes after AO3 went offline on Oct. 29 for what became a 17-day maintenance period. At the time, the Organization for Transformative Works (OTW), the nonprofit behind AO3, warned that restoration could take two to four weeks, leaving fanfiction readers and writers without access to one of fandom's most important online archives.

Sources indicate that AO3 finally returned on Nov. 15, though the site wasn't fully operational. User icons, imports from other sites, and downloads in formats other than HTML remained temporarily disabled as volunteers continued restoration efforts. The organization had previously warned that additional downtime could occur during the recovery process.

The prolonged outage prompted fans to look for other places to congregate online. Tumblr reported a 49 percent increase in upcoming sign-ups during the first several days of AO3's absence, compared with the preceding two weeks, underscoring just how central the fanfiction archive has become to fandom communities.

But the disruption exposed growing tensions between fanfiction writers and readers. As readers scrambled to find copies of their favorite stories, some began circulating shared Google Drives containing downloaded works, prompting backlash from authors who hadn't consented to their stories being redistributed. The controversy sparked a larger conversation about ownership, consent, and the expectations that have developed between writers and readers in online fandom communities.

It's unclear whether Thursday's preventative maintenance is directly connected to the earlier outage or how long the latest disruption will last. AO3 has not provided an estimated restoration time.

For fanfiction readers who only just got their favorite archive back, it's another unwelcome plot twist.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that grand Theft Auto VI follows Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos as a botched job drags them into a criminal conspiracy across Leonida, Rockstar's fictional version of Florida. But the most interesting details emerge from the people they encounter along the way — from smugglers in the Keys to rappers chasing stardom in Vice City.

Sources indicate that we've compiled the characters we know about so far, including those Rockstar introduced before launch, and other GTA 6 NPCs who've appeared in reviews, gameplay clips, and our own playthroughs. We'll keep updating this list as we discover more.

Spoiler alert: This article contains plot and character details about the missions, side quests, and characters of Grand Theft Auto VI.

Jason Duval — A former soldier who works for drug runners in the Leonida Keys. He wants an easier life, but when a job goes wrong, he and Lucia get caught up in a much bigger criminal conspiracy. He's also a pretty good dancer.

Lucia Caminos — Jason's partner in crime. Her father taught her to fight growing up, and after a stint in Leonida Penitentiary, she's determined to build a better life for herself.

Industry observers note that brian Heder — A veteran smuggler who runs his operation out of a boatyard and lets Jason live rent-free in exchange for helping with jobs. His wife Lori is also involved.

According to recent reports, cal Hampton — Jason's friend and one of Brian's associates. He listens in on Coast Guard communications and has questions about why birds fly in formation.

Donnie — A member of Brian's crew who helps with drug and package runs.

According to recent reports, mandy — One of Brian's tenants. Jason goes to collect her overdue rent in the early mission "Pipework" and winds up helping with repairs. Their flirty exchange swiftly made Mandy a launch-day fan favorite.

Shirley — Jason's neighbor in Key Lento. Her first request is a bottle of rum. Her second is a little more involved.

Peggy — Shirley's neighbor and the owner of the scooter Shirley wants Jason to steal. Peggy comes out to confront him when he tries to take it.

Dre'Quan Priest — An aspiring music mogul who books acts at Boobie’s club and signs Real Dimez.

Boobie Ike — The owner of the Jack of Hearts strip club and Dre'Quan's business partner at Only Raw Records.

Bae-Luxe and Roxy Rashad — High school friends who perform together as Real Dimez. They built a following with rap tracks and social media.

Raul Bautista — A seasoned bank robber always looking for people willing to take a chance on his next job.

Captain Aldo Méndez — A Vice City police officer who knows Jason and Lucia and takes part in a raid on Raymond's operation. Raymond — Jason and Lucia cross paths with him on a package pickup at the Venture Apartments.

Recent findings suggest that andrés de León — A VIP Jason and Lucia are hired to protect during a visit to Megamundo's U.S. headquarters.

Petra Navarro — Megamundo's chief operating officer, who appears in the Netflix extended gameplay preview.

Valentina — A fixer who appears in the Megamundo storyline.

Counselor Stefanie Gates — Lucia's correctional social worker at Leonida Penitentiary.

Bret Vogel — Jason's old Army friend, who teaches him to track deer and sends him on hunts.

Kenton Rees — Hires Jason to dive at a shipwreck.

Billy — A contact Jason can meet through a mud club, with several jobs that follow.

Andy — A character Lucia meets through the Cellerica side missions.

A very angry woman on a mobility scooter — An older woman appears to hold someone at gunpoint from her scooter. When the player steps in, she turns the gun on them, too.

A furry in a fox suit — While driving around as Lucia, a reviewer for Dexerto saw a police helicopter shine its spotlight on a man in a fox costume. They ended up helping him and his friends escape. Apparently, furries are where Leonida draws the line. (Seriously, there's apparently an anti-furry association in the game.).

Sources indicate that A Hulk-like red giant — IShowSpeed ran into a towering red figure who tossed people and cars around and took on the police. The encounter reportedly ended with a hug before the giant leapt into the sky. Fans pointed out the plotline's connection with the villain in Captain America: Brave Upcoming World.

Animal rights protestors — During one part of the game, a group stops a truck taking a bear to a zoo. In a separate encounter, an animal rights protest leads to the player helping free a group of caged apes. GTA 6 gameplay prevents you from killing any protestors (yes, people tried).

Sources indicate that parrot smugglers at a liquor store — One reviewer for Fast Tech giant came across a parrot-smuggling operation inside a liquor store. There's a side quest I wouldn’t have thought to look for, but GTA 6 is full of unexpected animal encounters.

According to recent reports, leonida's very own Bigfoot — Players on Reddit and X have been posting sightings of the Skunk Ape. In several clips, they find him near a dirt road with a deer carcass.

How to adjust and turn off motion blur in GTA 6 if it makes you feel sick

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (425 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If the blur makes you feel a little nauseous, there are settings to mitigate it.
  • If you've been waiting years to play Grand Theft Auto 6, nothing is more disappointing than booting it up and finding it doesn't look quite as good as you'd hoped—or worse, that it makes you feel sick.
  • According to recent reports, for some people, motion blur just doesn't look good.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If the blur makes you feel a little nauseous, there are settings to mitigate it.

If you've been waiting years to play Grand Theft Auto 6, nothing is more disappointing than booting it up and finding it doesn't look quite as good as you'd hoped—or worse, that it makes you feel sick. There are a number of things that could be causing that, but the good news is that one of the most common culprits is extremely easy to fix. Motion blur is a standard feature in most AAA games these days, but there are good reasons some players want to avoid it.

According to recent reports, for some people, motion blur just doesn't look good. GTA 6 is the most expensive game ever made, and one reason is its incredibly lifelike graphics. If a layer of motion blur on top of that ruins the illusion, that's enough of a reason to turn it off. Even worse, motion blur commonly contributes to motion sickness, causing dizziness and nausea in some players. Motion blur is nearly ubiquitous in modern games, but fortunately, there are usually settings to tone it down or turn it off completely.

Industry observers note that it's easy to adjust or turn off motion blur in GTA 6. Just pause the game and select Settings from the bottom of the main menu. Next, scroll over to the Display tab by pressing the right shoulder button. About halfway down the page, under the visual effects heading, you'll see a setting called Motion Blur Strength with a slider. By default, it's set to three out of 10, so you can actually tone down the effect without completely turning it off, or even increase it. You can also just set the strength to zero to turn off motion blur completely.

Recent findings suggest that it's worth playing with this setting a little bit to find the level that works for you. Especially at lower frame rates, motion blur can help smooth out camera movements that might otherwise be distractingly jittery, so even leaving it at its lowest level can help. Including a slider instead of a simple toggle is a welcome feature in GTA 6, letting you dial it in to your exact needs.

Since GTA 6 targets 30 fps on consoles, rather than 60 fps, those jarring camera movements may be a bigger deal than they are in other massive releases. The best level of motion blur for you will depend more on your TV and personal preference than anything else.

Latest Update: Commerce approved sales of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies, Rep. Mast indicates

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (789 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The subagency of the Commerce Department that regulates and enforces exports approved the sale of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies including Alibaba and Tencent as of May 2026, according to documents released Thursday by the House Foreign Affairs Committee.
  • Some of those approvals, made by Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security, included sales to companies designated by the Department of Defense as "Chinese Military Companies," according to the documents.
  • It has been revealed that "Over the past month, the administration's handling of chip export controls has put our national security and technology edge at risk.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The subagency of the Commerce Department that regulates and enforces exports approved the sale of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies including Alibaba and Tencent as of May 2026, according to documents released Thursday by the House Foreign Affairs Committee.

Some of those approvals, made by Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security, included sales to companies designated by the Department of Defense as "Chinese Military Companies," according to the documents. From December through May, there had been 3.4 million requested sales of U.S. AI chips to China, the committee reported, citing those made by Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices.

It has been revealed that "Over the past month, the administration's handling of chip export controls has put our national security and technology edge at risk. The Bureau of Industry and Security has failed to enforce the rules, and Congress must now conduct rigorous oversight of the administration's policies," Rep. Gregory Meeks, D-N.Y., the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, remarked at a meeting of the panel Thursday at which members voted to release the documents.

The Commerce Department, AMD and Nvidia did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

"The license information we are disclosing today will help inform the American public about how BIS has handled licenses for Nvidia H200 and equivalent AMD chips to China. The public has the right to know how these decisions were made," Meeks continued.

According to recent reports, the committee cited the Export Control Reform Act as justification for releasing the data. The panel stated the law allows it to declassify and release export data if it "determines that the withholding of the following information is contrary to the national interest."The license requests released by the Foreign Affairs Committee include requests to sell to major firms including Bytedance, Tesla (Shanghai) and Baidu.

The release of documents comes in the wake of Jensen Huang's resignation from the chip supplier Nvidia after news surfaced that he had several extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy that led to concerns about Nvidia chips being diverted to China.

In the weeks since, Republicans and Democrats in Congress have called for legislation to be passed that would impose stricter export controls on the sale of advanced AI chips to China and other adversaries.

Mast noted two of the firms listed in Nvidia license applications to BIS — Maginfra and Newly introduced Matrix — are suspected "smuggling fronts." The New York Times reported in November that both companies had empty offices and had ties to companies under national security sanctions.

"Both are fake companies. If BIS approved the sale of these chips to these firms, obviously that is of tremendous concern to us — especially given that President Trump made clear last year that the sale of any AI chips to China will have very real national security conditions," Mast mentioned at the Thursday meeting.

Maginfra and New Matrix did not immediately reply to requests for comment.

Recent findings suggest that shares of AMD fell Thursday after the investment firm Hunterbrook Media issued a report alleging the company "has its own China problem." The report claims that "after the U.S. blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, the company kept getting newer AMD firmware, which enables AMD chips to run in servers.".

CNBC did not independently verify this information.

Fallout from the Huang scandal on Capitol Hill has intensified in the last week, as lawmakers question the degree to which the former head of Nvidia's relationship with the suspected Chinese spy could have jeopardized national security and American AI dominance.

Huang is due for a closed-door transcribed interview with the House Foreign Affairs panel and two other committees on Dec. 1. Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter is scheduled to appear before the panels Dec. 2.

Senate banking committee Chair Tim Scott, R-S.C., announced on CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Wednesday that Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick had also agreed to testify.

Lutnick has come under fire over his relationship to Huang and for his failure to take action on Megaspeed, the Singaporean manufacturer where Alice Huang, with whom the former Nvidia CEO had an affair, was an executive until 2025. U.S. investigators suspect Megaspeed diverted Nvidia chips to China.

Amid that criticism, the Commerce Department on Monday issued an interim final rule to close a loophole that has allowed Chinese companies lease Nvidia's advancing computing power from data centers in third controls.

The rule was "written by and at the direction of" the Treasury Department and the White House National Security Council, BIS said in a press release.

#1537. Breaking: Anthropic’s IPO puts AI’s circular financing boom to the test

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1121 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 TechCrunch ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Anthropic’s IPO puts AI’s circular financing boom to the test

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1121 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arriving at public markets today, Anthropic’s IPO is poised to raise billions for the organization and its investors.
  • Industry observers note that amazon and Google, two of Anthropic’s largest infrastructure partners, hold stakes valued around a combined $307.9 billion at the tech giant’s updated IPO price of $83 per share.
  • Sources indicate that A handful of other AI infrastructure providers are also positioned to benefit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arriving at public markets today, Anthropic’s IPO is poised to raise billions for the organization and its investors. But the biggest surprise may be just how much of that money will end up going to supplier-investors.

Industry observers note that amazon and Google, two of Anthropic’s largest infrastructure partners, hold stakes valued around a combined $307.9 billion at the tech giant’s updated IPO price of $83 per share. Amazon, which invested $18 billion into the AI startup, would see its 14.7% stake hit upwards of $159 billion, while Google’s 13.7% stake is valued at nearly $149 billion, according to share ownership figures disclosed in Anthropic’s IPO prospectus.

Sources indicate that A handful of other AI infrastructure providers are also positioned to benefit. Nvidia, AMD, Microsoft, Broadcom, Micron, and TSMC have joined Google in committing $26 billion to Anthropic at its IPO price in a private placement.

In total, Google has invested $12.3 billion into Anthropic since 2023, with another promised $30 billion dependent on Anthropic meeting certain performance milestones. And with the exception of TSMC, Anthropic has unveiled multibillion-dollar strategic partnerships with its other infrastructure supplier investors — including Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Microsoft, and Micron — that would see Anthropic purchasing their products.

This is the circular financing that has made some observers so skeptical of the AI boom. These companies are not just investors; they’re also Anthropic’s biggest suppliers. It might look like Amazon and Google are putting billions into Anthropic, but they get that money right back when Anthropic needs to train a model or serve Claude to customers. From afar, it looks like unprecedented revenue growth for cloud companies and unprecedented fundraising from Anthropic — but it’s just the same money passing from one pocket to another.

Today’s IPO marks a critical change in that financing system, the moment it might just become self-sustaining. Those investments appear to have paid off, and are now liquid. Anthropic is still operating at a net loss of tens of billions of dollars each quarter — but it will no longer be suppliers and private investors footing the bill. Now, capital will come from a mix of public-market investors and corporate bonds, neither of which have the conflicts-of-interest that caused concerns before.

And critically, the firm’s new bottom line looks pretty good.

Once it debuts, Anthropic is expected to have about $220 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments, including proceeds from its IPO and the $26 billion private placement. Anthropic also has the ability to pay for future commitments in stock.

Joey Brookhart, who leads the Tokenomics team at SemiAnalysis, estimates that Anthropic needs roughly $280 billion in cumulative revenue over the next four years to pay for its compute bill, which Brookhart mentioned is “achievable given where they will be next year from a revenue perspective.”.

Sources indicate that “The ownership stake is very worthwhile, and those companies no longer need any more support from [suppliers],” Brookhart told TechCrunch. “Amazon doesn’t need to prop them up anymore. The revenue is all coming from other customers.”.

That doesn’t mean the server bills are going down, though. Anthropic has already committed to spend $900 billion, primarily for compute and infrastructure, according to a regulatory filing. Certain agreements have termination provisions, but Brookhart thinks the organization is in a strong position to pay up.

On the other side, Anthropic generated $17 billion in third-quarter 2026 revenue, putting the company on pace for a $68 billion annualized rate for the year. If Anthropic continues to grow at its current trajectory, Brookhart believes it could easily cover the gap needed to fund its compute.

It has been revealed that gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson, agreed.

It has been revealed that “By the time the IPO is done, Anthropic’s going to have more cash on hand than any manufacturer has ever had,” Luria told TechCrunch, noting that the firm raised around $141 billion in capital and will take home around $91.7 billion in net proceeds at $83 per share. “And they’re not burning cash. They’re just going to have a war chest.”.

In a recent development, A public listing will make Anthropic a more credible borrower, making it easier to raise money outside of public markets, claims Brookhart. That’s despite recent reports that creditors might not see Anthropic as “investment-grade” material.

Luria distinguished between Anthropic’s supplier investments and neoclouds like CoreWeave, which he sees as more purely supported by circular financing. “CoreWeave wouldn’t exist if Nvidia didn’t prop them up, and it probably won’t exist if Nvidia doesn’t bail them out,” Luria mentioned.

Brookhart also pushed back on describing Anthropic’s financing as purely circular, saying it was still “additive to the ecosystem.”.

It has been revealed that for both analysts, the biggest risk to Anthropic is simply that it will lose the AI race. Right now, the firm’s growth is fueled by its status at the frontier of generative AI — but if it’s overtaken by OpenAI, Google DeepMind, or even cheap open-weight models, that could change fast. As Luria put it: “If we’re all using other people’s models, then Anthropic’s not worth a trillion and a half dollars. It’s worth nothing.”.

But regardless of who wins the frontier, compute suppliers will likely be just fine. Neither Brookhart nor Luria believe Anthropic’s growth is at risk, despite some arguments that cheaper tokens and more competition will directly affect the AI organization’s bottom line.

Industry observers note that “For Amazon and Google, the risk isn’t actually that high because in that scenario, we’re using other models,” Luria noted. “I’m arguing we’re going to use a lot more AI. I don’t know if it’s all Anthropic’s AI…. That’s still going to come from a data center managed by Amazon, Google, and Microsoft.”.

After a string of tech outages and hacks, many Americans are on alert. And on Thursday, the Wall Street Journal reported that a ransomware group had leaked the data of thousands of customers at JPMorgan Chase, Mastercard, and Visa.

Crucially, all of the companies have said that no credit card numbers or customer funds were compromised in the cyberattack. The companies' financial services are all operating normally, and JPMorgan Chase released a statement on X confirming the hack is unrelated to a Chase Bank outage earlier this week.

The leak contained some customers' names and email addresses, according to JPMorgan Chase.

According to recent reports, for its part, a Mastercard representative told Mashable that the incident "resulted in the exposure of a limited amount of email addresses — non-payments information — from a small subset of cardholders enrolled in a specific benefit program." Customers can continue to use their cards as normal. The spokesperson added, "At this time, the exposure has been contained and our teams are working with the provider to support the impacted cardholders as needed." Not only that, but SOCRadar found that n0n has also claimed to have compromised data at major organizations including Airbnb, Starbucks, EssilorLuxottica, Procter & Gamble, Walmart, and AARP — all in the past three days.

Apple fires back at Epic over claims it withheld 122,000 documents

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple has responded to Epic Games’ filing from last Friday, pushing back against accusations that it improperly withheld more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions.
  • While the Supreme Court is set to review whether the civil contempt designation against Apple should be upheld in its lawsuit against Epic Games, the two companies have also been battling in the district court over what commission, if any, Apple should be allowed to charge on purchases made through external payment systems.
  • Apple submitted its proposal to the district court on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, but Epic is disputing not just the basis for those proposed rates, but also Apple’s handling of document production in the proceedings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple has responded to Epic Games’ filing from last Friday, pushing back against accusations that it improperly withheld more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions. Here are the details.

While the Supreme Court is set to review whether the civil contempt designation against Apple should be upheld in its lawsuit against Epic Games, the two companies have also been battling in the district court over what commission, if any, Apple should be allowed to charge on purchases made through external payment systems.

Apple submitted its proposal to the district court on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, but Epic is disputing not just the basis for those proposed rates, but also Apple’s handling of document production in the proceedings.

As part of the proceedings, Epic had submitted 16 categories of documents it wanted Apple to produce (including “internal analyses of the financial or business impact” of its proposed commissions and “communications relating to any strategies to dissuade developers from offering link-outs”), along with a list of current and former Apple employees whose records should be searched.

Apple agreed to use Epic’s proposed search terms and include all employees, and began producing documents it determined were responsive to Epic’s requests.

Epic, however, mentioned last Friday that Apple was improperly withholding more than 122,000 documents matching those search terms from the records of the seven initial employees, and asked the court to order Apple to produce all matching non-privileged documents, regardless of its relevance assessments.

Which brings us to Apple’s newest filing.

In its filing, Apple argues that contrary to Epic’s claim that its proposed search terms were “tailored” to the proceedings over link-out fees, they were actually “overbroad,” capturing large numbers of unrelated documents.

For instance, Apple notes that while intended to identify documents related to its proposed commission rates, Epic’s “commission*” search term also “captures documents that refer to government and private commissions, as well as documents hitting on the totally irrelevant term ‘commissioner,’ such as documents discussing the NFL Commissioner.”.

“[…] the use of a wildcard in a search string is designated by the asterisk symbol, which means that the search string will hit on any term that includes the prefix before the asterisk.

In the same vein, Apple notes that “Epic’s use of ‘fee*’ in its search strings related to litigation and Apple’s link-out-related projects pulled in documents containing words like ‘feel,’ ‘feed,’ ‘feedback,’ ‘feet,’ and ‘feeble’ without the word ‘fee’ or ‘fees’ appearing at all.”.

Apple’s overall argument is that these unrelated matches account for the vast majority of documents identified by Epic’s searches, and it cites legal precedent to argue that it should only be required to produce documents responsive to Epic’s requests, rather than every document matching the agreed-upon search terms:.

In fact, at least 95% of the Initial Custodian Document Population hit on generic terms like these and did not include any reference to the term “link-out” or its variations, despite that concept being central to the Proffer and related discovery. These sweeping terms do not just increase the total volume of the Initial Custodian Document Population, they also captured highly sensitive and irrelevant documents, such as Apple employees’ personal tax or financial records, medical records, documents discussing unannounced products, documents containing passwords, investor-relations materials, and privileged or protected legal communications.

Industry observers note that the law is clear: parties are only required to produce responsive documents, not every document returned by a search string. […] (“The Court will not compel defendants to produce any document simply because it contains a search term whether or not it is responsive to the discovery request.”). Epic has not shown, and cannot show, why the regular discovery process should be disrupted here. Speculation based on hit counts, particularly where the producing party can explain low responsiveness rates, does not justify the extraordinary and unprecedented remedy Epic seeks.

Apple goes on to argue that complying with Epic’s demands would require extensive additional work, including reviewing documents for privileged or sensitive information and redacting protected material, making it impossible to meet Epic’s proposed December 2 deadline.

Finally, Apple asks the court to reject Epic’s motion but proposes that, should the court decide that some intervention is warranted, a randomized, statistically significant sample of the documents it deems nonresponsive be submitted to a Special Master for independent review, rather than producing all of them to Epic directly.

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 6 gives players lots of ways to customize the experience, from the clothes the protagonists wear to granular user interface controls. Being able to shift your perspective of the action is part of that. Rockstar has long offered GTA players the ability to reposition the camera, and you can do that this time around as well.

In the camera tab of the settings menu, you can adjust the height of the camera while you're on foot, as well as the horizontal and vertical follow speeds. You have similar options for land and water vehicles, along with specific follow speeds based on whether you're the driver or a passenger. When it comes to aircraft, you can adjust the follow speed and determine whether the camera follows your plane when you do a barrel roll.

It has been revealed that when you're out there exploring the map in a land or water vehicle, you can change the height of the camera on the fly. To switch between the three options, hold the down button on the D-pad, pick the height you want and confirm. You'll also be able to switch to the cinematic camera mode here. This makes things like high-speed chases look cool, but you might find it harder to steer your vehicle.

In addition, there are some very limited ways in which you can switch to a first-person perspective. While you're on foot, you can hold the left trigger on your controller and click the right thumbstick. This lets you take a closer look at your surroundings.

Sources indicate that going back to the camera section of the settings menu, you can enable a first-person perspective when your character is looking at their phone. If you look at your phone while you're driving (in GTA 6, never in real life), you'll see your device and the road from a first-person view as well. Perhaps Rockstar will add a proper first-person mode to GTA 6 down the line, as it did with the previous game.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • government has been ordered to confirm that it issued a secret order demanding Apple to provide authorities with encrypted customer information.
  • The Thursday ruling from the U.K.’s Investigatory Powers Tribunal, an independent court that allows citizens to challenge government surveillance orders, is a rare rebuke for the government, which sought to keep the encryption backdoor order a state secret.
  • The tribunal’s ruling rejected the Home Office’s claim that disclosing the order would be damaging to national security.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the U.K. government has been ordered to confirm that it issued a secret order demanding Apple to provide authorities with encrypted customer information.

The Thursday ruling from the U.K.’s Investigatory Powers Tribunal, an independent court that allows citizens to challenge government surveillance orders, is a rare rebuke for the government, which sought to keep the encryption backdoor order a state secret.

The tribunal’s ruling rejected the Home Office’s claim that disclosing the order would be damaging to national security.

Industry observers note that the ruling comes a year after the U.K. government reportedly demanded that Apple build a backdoor to allow U.K. authorities access to customer data anywhere in the world. Details of the so-called “technical capabilities notice,” which are issued under strict non-disclosure rules, leaked to the media, which drew ire from White House officials and U.S. lawmakers who criticized the effort, arguing that the U.K. order would put Americans’ privacy at risk.

In a recent development, california-based Apple refused the order, and blocked U.K. users from switching on its Advanced Data Protection data-encryption feature for iCloud, rather than comply with the demand. The U.K.’s secret order was later narrowed to allow access to British nationals’ data stored in Apple’s encrypted cloud, and Apple also challenged this second order.

Industry observers note that prior to the ruling, Apple was legally barred from disclosing the order, even after details leaked. When reached for comment, Apple told TechCrunch that it welcomes the decision to make public the fact that the U.K. Home Office issued a technical capability notice.

Apple previously mentioned that it has “never built a backdoor or master key” to any of its products or services and “never will.”.

A spokesperson for the U.K. Home Office, which has yet to confirm the existence of a notice, did not respond to a request for comment.

Rights group Liberty International, which brought the legal challenge on behalf of two individuals, stated that this is the first known time that the government has been compelled to confirm the existence of a secret technical order.

A final hearing on what specific order details can be released is anticipated next year.
